manual.title: Add a manual alert
manual.description: A manual alert is fired and dismissed by the `alert_redux.fire` and `alert_redux.dismiss` actions.

data_description.name: Shown on the card and used as the notification title. The entity ID is derived from it when the alert is created.
data_description.priority: Sets the alert's colour and sort order.
data_description.icon: Leave empty to use the priority's default icon.
data_description.acknowledgeable: Turn off for alerts that must not be silenced.
data_description.user_dismissable: Show a dismiss button on the card. The dismiss action always works, whatever this is set to.
data_description.subject_entity: Optional. The entity the alert is about, for use in messages. Leave empty to use the watched entity, if there is one.

notifications.name: Notifications and messages
notifications.description: Who is notified, how often reminders are sent, and what the messages say.

data_description.use_default_groups: Send to the default notifier groups set in the integration's options. Turn off to choose this alert's own groups.
data_description.notifier_groups: Used when the default groups are turned off. Leave empty to notify nobody.
data_description.use_default_reminders: Use the default reminder schedule set in the integration's options. Turn off to set this alert's own.
data_description.reminder_schedule: Used when the default schedule is turned off. Minutes between reminders while the alert is firing and unacknowledged, e.g. `10, 20, 30, 60`: the last gap repeats. Leave empty for no reminders.
data_description.use_default_throttle: Use the default throttle set in the integration's options. Turn off to set this alert's own.
data_description.throttle_count: Used when the default throttle is turned off. At most this many on notifications in any window of the minutes below; the one that reaches the limit is marked "[Throttling starts]", later ones and done notifications are held, and a summary is sent when the rate drops. Leave both empty for no throttling.
data_description.message: Optional. Sent when the alert starts firing, and shown on the card. A template: it can use `name`, `subject_entity_name`, `fire_count`, `fire_data`, `duration`, and entity states. Leave empty for the default: the alert's name, followed by "is firing."
data_description.display_message: Optional. A different message for the card, if the on message isn't what you want shown there. Also a template.
data_description.reminder_message: Optional. Sent as a reminder while the alert is still firing. A template, as for the on message; `duration` is how long it has been firing. Leave empty for the default, which gives the name and that duration.
data_description.done_message: Optional. Sent when the alert stops firing. A template, as for the on message; `duration` is how long it fired, and `end_reason` is `resolved`, `dismissed`, or `no_data`. Leave empty for the default.
data_description.buttons: Optional. Buttons on this alert's mobile app notifications, each running an action, e.g. a *Close door* button that closes the garage door. Only the configured action runs. On and reminder notifications carry them, followed by the built-in *Acknowledge* and *Snooze* (unless the alert can't be acknowledged); Android shows the first three. A button still runs its action after the alert has stopped firing.
data_description.button_snooze_duration: Optional. How long the notification's *Snooze* button snoozes this alert. Leave empty to use the default from the integration's options.

supersession.name: Supersession
supersession.description: Alerts this one takes precedence over. While this alert is firing, they don't send on or reminder notifications, and if they stop firing together with it, only this alert's done notification is sent.

data_description.supersedes: Optional. The alerts this one supersedes. Supersession is transitive: an alert superseded by one of these is superseded by this one too. For each, choose what acknowledging it does to this alert: nothing; acknowledge this alert, even before it fires; or snooze it, for the duration counted from that acknowledgement.

state.title: Add a state alert

data_description.subject_entity: Optional. The entity the alert is about, for use in messages. Leave empty to use the watched entity, if there is one.
data_description.no_data_grace: Optional. How long a firing alert keeps firing while its inputs have no data. Leave empty to use the global default.

ack.description: Acknowledges a firing alert, stopping its reminders until it stops firing. Acknowledging a snoozed alert keeps it acknowledged when the snooze would have run out.

default_groups_unset.title: No default notifier groups are set
default_groups_unset.description:
{count} alerts use the default notifier groups, but none are set, so their notifications go to the fallback instead (a persistent notification, unless you've chosen a fallback group): {alerts}.

To fix this, add a notifier group, then choose it as a default in the Alert Redux integration's options (Settings > Devices & services > Alert Redux > Configure). Alternatively, give each alert its own notifier groups.

notify_action_missing.title: Notifier group {group} uses a missing action
notify_action_missing.description:
The notifier group **{group}** sends to `{action}`, but that action doesn't exist, so it can't be notified. Notifications still reach the group's other members, or the fallback if none of them can be notified.

Integrations are gradually replacing their legacy notify actions with notify entities. If that has happened here, edit the group to use the notify entity instead. If the action should exist, check the integration that provides it. This issue clears itself once the action exists again or the group no longer uses it.

broken_reference.title: An alert refers to an alert that doesn't exist
broken_reference.description:
The alert {alert} refers to {missing}, which doesn't exist: it was deleted or renamed, or its generator no longer makes it.

{alert} keeps working, failing towards more notifications rather than fewer: it no longer suppresses or is suppressed by the missing alert, acknowledgements aren't passed on, and an alert state alert watching it has no data.

To fix this, edit {alert} to remove or replace the reference, or recreate the missing alert. This issue goes away by itself once the reference is fixed.
